name: Dub

attributes.attribute: Irish heroine or goddess and a bard and druid
pool of Dub, a deep pool in the mouth of the River Liffey
weapon that killed Dub in revenge
founders who called the town Dyflinasrski
bitter-tongued bard who built the wicker bridge

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Dub is an Irish heroine or goddess. The capital city of Ireland is named for her. Dublin rose from older names, Dubhlinn and Dubh-linn. Dubh-linn means the pool of Dub. A deep pool sat in the mouth of the River Liffey. Dub fell there after a slingshot killed her. The shot came in revenge. Dub had drowned a woman her husband consorted with. Dubh also means dark, so the city reads as dark pool. Dub was a bard and a druid woman. Norsemen founded the town and called it Dyflinasrski. In Irish the city is Baile Átha Cliath. That name means the town on the wicker ford. The bard Aithirne built the wicker bridge.
